'''Antoine Roger Rigaudeau''' (born 17 December 1971) is a French former professional [[basketball]] player and professional [[basketball coach]].  During his playing days, he played at the [[point guard]], [[shooting guard]], and [[small forward]] positions. Also during his playing career, his nickname was "Le Roi" ("The King").<ref>[http://www.fibaeurope.com/compID_MsfTeemRHYovSUdkYV76x0.season_1992.roundID_2547.coid_JwG3xYXrJzozQq4LNrX3u0.articleMode_on.html FRENCH GREAT "LE ROI" RETIRES.]</ref>

During his pro [[sports club|club]] career, he won two [[EuroLeague]] championships, in [[1998 EuroLeague Final Four|1998]] and [[2001 EuroLeague Finals|2001]]. With the [[France national basketball team|France national team]], he won the [[silver medal]] at the [[Basketball at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2000 Olympics]]. He was inducted into the [[French Basketball Hall of Fame]] in 2010. He became a [[FIBA Hall of Famer|FIBA Hall of Fame player]] in 2015.<ref>[https://www.fiba.basketball/news/2015-class-of-fiba-hall-of-fame-antoine-rigaudeau 2015 Class of FIBA Hall of Fame: Antoine Rigaudeau.]</ref>

==Professional career==
===Europe===
Rigaudeau won the [[LNB Pro A|French Pro A League]] championship with [[Élan Béarnais Pau-Orthez|Pau-Orthez]], in 1996. With [[Pallacanestro Virtus Bologna|Virtus Bologna]], he won the [[EuroLeague]] championship in the [[1998 EuroLeague Final Four|EuroLeague 1997–98]] and [[2001 EuroLeague Final Four|EuroLeague 2000–01]] seasons. With the same club, he also played in the EuroLeague Finals in [[1999 EuroLeague Final Four|1999]] and [[2002 EuroLeague Final Four|2002]]. With Virtus Bologna, he also won two [[Lega Basket Serie A|Italian Serie A League]] championships, in 1998 and 2001; and three [[Italian Basketball Cup|Italian Cup]] titles, in 1999, 2001, and 2002.

===NBA===
Rigaudeau played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) with the [[Dallas Mavericks]], during their [[2002–03 Dallas Mavericks season|2002–03 season]], after he signed a three-year contract with the club, on 17 January 2003.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.michigansthumb.com/news/article/Mavs-Complete-Paperwork-to-Sign-Rigaudeau-7367794.php |title=Mavs Complete Paperwork to Sign Rigaudeau. |access-date=2020-05-26 |archive-date=2020-06-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200621013901/https://www.michigansthumb.com/news/article/Mavs-Complete-Paperwork-to-Sign-Rigaudeau-7367794.php |url-status=dead }}</ref> With the Mavericks, he played in a total of 11 games, and averaged 1.5 points, 0.7 rebounds, and 0.5 assists per game, in 8.3 minutes played per game.<ref name=bbr/> On 18 August 2003, the Mavericks traded Rigaudeau's player rights to the [[Golden State Warriors]], prior to the start of the [[2003–04 NBA season]].<ref>[https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/trade_8_18_03.html Warriors Acquire Nick Van Exel, Four Others From Dallas Mavericks.]</ref> On 5 September 2003, the Warriors released Rigaudeau.

===Return to Europe===
After being released by the [[Golden State Warriors]], Rigaudeau returned to Europe, and joined the [[Liga ACB|Spanish ACB League]] club [[Valencia Basket|Valencia]]. He officially retired from playing pro [[sports club|club]] basketball in 2005, after he had previously suffered an [[Achilles tendon]] injury on his left foot.

==National team career==
Rigaudeau was a member of the senior [[France national basketball team|France national team]]. He represented France at the [[1991 EuroBasket]], the [[1993 EuroBasket]], the [[1995 EuroBasket]], and the [[1999 EuroBasket]]. With France, he won the silver medal at the [[Basketball at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2000 Olympics]].

In 2001, before that year's [[2001 EuroBasket|EuroBasket]] tournament, Rigaudeau retired from playing with the senior France national team. However, he later decided to rejoin the national team for the [[2005 EuroBasket]], where he won the bronze medal. He retired again from the France national team after that tournament. He had a total of 127 [[cap (sports)|appearances]] with France's senior national team.

==Coaching career==
Rigaudeau began his professional [[basketball coach|coaching]] career in 2015, when he became the [[head coach]] of the [[LNB Pro A|French Pro A League]] club [[Paris-Levallois Basket|Paris-Levallois]], which was later renamed to Metropolitans 92.
